releaseIntent: Finish one bounded open-source v1.2 release by reducing the product to its portable collaboration kernel, host-admission standard, representative help-and-interference evaluation and two thin reference projections. Release is a maintained baseline for later field learning, not an assertion of universal or final human-AI collaboration effectiveness.

activeIncrement.observedProblem: The sound goal-first collaboration proposition accumulated host-specific proof machinery, duplicated prose authority and generation-specific validators. Two months of honest Codex-led trial and correction exposed repair-by-addition, proof-proxy, context and topology burden, stale evidence replay and cleanup failure modes. A clean historical verifier now fails by replaying superseded O1 evidence, demonstrating that the proof path can obstruct the current product. The first GT-02 dirty-repository run then exposed hidden Python cache residue, and the same cleanup failure repeated after one minimal instruction repair; this proves that an observed host failure must narrow host qualification rather than trigger another prompt layer or be misclassified as Harness release failure. Post-reshape adversarial review then reproduced repository-self-authorized release completion, out-of-root absence probes, expanded install or execution surfaces and partial projection-identity replay.
activeIncrement.hypothesis: A small K1-K5 portable kernel, H1-H10 host-admission standard, L1-L7 learned-failure standard, one data-driven verifier, representative help-and-interference Golden Tasks and thin Codex and Claude projections can preserve the useful lessons, distinguish Harness conformance from host behavior qualification, and cut default complexity enough to produce a finite, reproducible v1.2 release.
falsifiers: the reshape creates a new runtime, registry, router, ledger, context predictor or generic control plane
historical O1-O5 validators or evidence remain on the default verification path
the verifier duplicates product prose or derives success from implementation, tests, receipts, commits or report shape
the Codex or Claude projection requires a long mandatory profile, fixed host version, universal context threshold or user-operated capability or topology route
a representative task failure is hidden, promoted into a pass, erased by evaluator cleanup, or left without an exact host claim limit and residue disposition
a material shortfall invariant or two-month counterexample disappears rather than becoming a compact rule, test or explicit claim limit
tracked active code, product-test and primary-instruction complexity does not materially fall from the pre-reshape baseline
release or field-effect is claimed before its exact evidence and named-human authority
repository data grants human authority, an absence locator escapes the repository, or a Skill-only package admits an undeclared install, runtime or execution surface
activeIncrement.finiteStopCondition: The three authority files validate; the old proof generations leave the active tree; one generic verifier and both thin host projections map the same K, H, L, R and Q contract; the finite representative sample records help, interference, pass and failure without stale projection replay; every failure narrows the exact host claim; evaluator-owned residue is absent; the exact candidate and claim ceiling receive named-human release authorization. Field-effect and cross-host or longitudinal lanes remain explicitly continuing after release.

deliverables: one generic verifier and instant host-admission command
two thin progressively disclosed host projections
project-audit custody and shared-research revision reference
small public documentation and release-candidate evidence
workItems.stopCondition: A clean checkout reproduces all required deterministic checks, the exact finite representative sample and all pass/failure decisions are independently reviewable, failed host behaviors are excluded from the release claim, complexity targets pass, evaluator-owned residue is absent and the candidate waits only for the named human release decision.

goalModePrompt.objective: 在当前三份产品权威、项目专项审计和具名的人机协作短板研究约束下，将 Agent Autonomy Harness v1.2 收缩并完成为 K1-K5 可移植协作内核、H1-H10 即时宿主准入标准、L1-L7 试错经验标准、Codex/Claude 薄投影和可复现的帮助与干扰 Golden Tasks；真实完成 R1-R4 与 Q1-Q4 所需的有限开源发布证据和具名人类发布授权，同时把跨宿主、长期场景与真实场域价值保留为发布后持续校准和迭代。不得把报告、计划、提示词、代码、测试、提交、推送、转场、历史证据或局部通过称为收官；不得用加层掩盖重复失败；必须保留可迁移反例、控制过程损失、诚实限制主张并清理任务残留。
goalModePrompt.hostLifecycleNote: This repository value prepares the next exact objective. It does not claim that a paused host goal has been resumed or replaced.

complexityBudget.rule: Every retained mechanism must pay rent in observed help, risk reduction or recovery value after code, prompt, evidence, topology, cognition and lifecycle cost. A failed target blocks Q3 rather than inviting a larger verifier.

processLossControl.carrierRule: Use current source-bound host signals when reliable; if capacity is unavailable, record unknown and transition conservatively. No universal turn count, context size, token percentage or summary ratio is product authority.
processLossControl.correctionRule: A repeated correction or failed same-purpose mechanism pauses further addition until the premise, interface and deletion option are reconsidered.
processLossControl.continuingCalibration: Post-release failures may update Golden Tasks, narrow a claim, simplify or retire a projection, or open one new bounded increment; release status does not freeze learning.
